units.title: Normalized density TV and Hellinger affinity
units.reader_note: One common density comparison is shown first; its intrinsic density conditions, formula proof and exact Lean are folded below.
units.statement: Two normalized nonnegative densities satisfy both sharp TV–affinity comparisons.
assumptions: \((X,\mathcal A,\mu)\) is any measure space. No finiteness, probability or sigma-finiteness assumption is made on the reference measure \(\mu\).

\(f,g:X\to\mathbb R\) are measurable, nonnegative at every point, genuinely integrable, and satisfy \(\int f\,d\mu=\int g\,d\mu=1\). These define the generic density contract; the actual paper theorem has none of them as additional caller hypotheses.

This is a pointwise representative contract, not a claim of the weakest a.e. interface. Event masses are the actual density set integrals; actual-law consumers must identify them with the matching measures.

notation.text: Affinity uses a real Bochner integral; its true L1 and range are conclusions. The event supremum is over measurable sets only.

steps.title: Place square-root densities in L2
steps.text: The squared square roots are the original nonnegative densities. Their squared integrals are one. Cauchy–Schwarz gives both genuine integrability of their product and affinity at most one; its nonnegative integrand gives the other endpoint.
steps.formula: F=\sqrt f,\ G=\sqrt g,\quad\int F^2=\int G^2=1,\quad FG=\sqrt{fg}\in L^1,\quad0\le a\le1.
steps.lean: hF/hG use memLp_two_iff_integrable_sq. hmul uses MemLp.integrable_mul; hprod uses Real.sqrt_mul; ha1 uses integral_mul_le_Lp_mul_Lq_of_nonneg.

steps.title: Obtain the sharp half factor on every event
steps.text: Let d=f−g. It has total integral zero, so an event integral and its complement have opposite values. Bound the absolute integral on each part by the corresponding integral of |d| and add. The event-value set is nonempty and bounded.
steps.lean: hd0 follows from the unit masses; hevent uses integral_add_compl and abs_integral_le_integral_abs. hDne/hDbd and csSup_le produce the upper bound for the supremum.

steps.title: Attain the bound on the positive set
steps.text: The measurable set where d≥0 attains the positive-part integral. Since the total integral vanishes, the positive part is half the L1 norm. This proves equality with normalized event TV.
steps.lean: hpos identifies the positive part with B.indicator d. hattain uses integral_abs_eq_two_mul_integral_posPart_sub_integral and integral_indicator. le_csSup and hsup_le give htv.

steps.title: Derive the lower affinity comparison
steps.text: For nonnegative values, the smaller of f and g is at most their geometric mean. Equivalently, f+g−2√(fg)≤|f−g|. Integrate this inequality and use both masses and the exact TV identity.
steps.lean: hpoint uses Real.le_sqrt_of_sq_le in the two value orderings; hlower applies integral_mono with actual L1 of every term.

steps.title: Derive the upper affinity comparison
steps.text: Factor the density difference through the sum and difference of square roots. Their squares integrate to 2±2a. Cauchy–Schwarz, followed by nonnegative square-root algebra, gives the upper bound.
steps.lean: hminus/hplus establish L2; hminusInt/hplusInt expand the integrals. hc is the same canonical Mathlib Cauchy–Schwarz node, hfactor and hroot give the exact algebra, and hupper concludes.

units.lean_statement: Exact sealed generic normalized-density interface; none of its density conditions is exported by the actual Gaussian source theorem.
units.lean_proof: The exact extracted proof derives L1/range, normalized event TV equality and both comparisons, with all helpers local.
units.boundary: Generic normalized-density TV/affinity inequalities only. No Gaussian assumption/statement strengthened, no actual product law/tensorization or full main bounds, no new implication from analogy. Actual source adapter and Eq25 remain separate consumer obligations.

sources.anchor: Canonical common-measure-space normalized-density theorem; source motivation B.2.3 Ex68–69 and the leading TV/min/affinity comparison in Ex72. This is an explicit library generalization, not the paper statement on arbitrary spaces.

sources.scope: Any measurable carrier and common measure; two pointwise nonnegative measurable genuine L1 functions of mass one. Gaussian and actual product-law consumers must supply these conditions internally.
